## Plan: playable path to refugee crisis **start** (Feb 2302)

Goal: a new player can advance from **January 2300 → January 2302**, hit the major story beats, and see **`refugees_titan`** fire as the crisis opener without dead ends or silent broken systems.

### Phase A — Core loop hygiene (blocking)

1. ~~**Advance `phase` beyond 1**~~ — **Done:** [`cable_break_negotiations`](source/scenes/major/cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry) sets `phase = 2` when ≥2 megacorps accept the ceasefire (Jun 2301). Optionally tie [`organize_phase_tick`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) trade-level `phase` bands to calendar elsewhere.
2. ~~**Remove SPD leftovers**~~ — **Done:** deleted [`shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry`](source/scenes/cards/city_affairs/shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry). **Next:** design a `#city_affairs` card to renegotiate corp control of civil rights, judiciary, and related government levers (see table above).
3. **Fix [`organize_phase_start`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_start.scene.dry) entry** — Either gate it to Jan 2300 month 1 (first `post_event`) or chain explicitly from [`root`](source/scenes/root.scene.dry) `@2300_main_continue` so `organizing_unlock` is guaranteed before October events.
4. **Date-gate [`drone_vote_buying`](source/scenes/background/drone_vote_buying.dry)** — Add `year`, `max-visits`, or remove until designed; avoid firing every December forever.

### Phase B — 2300–2301 story spine (content)

5. ~~**September Convention fallout**~~ — **Done:** [`september_convention`](source/scenes/events/september_convention.scene.dry) permit bumps `parochialism`; ban cuts `parochialism` / `parochial_radicalism` and stacks `first_wave_ban_slights` (first-stratum poll modifiers in [`electorate_runtime`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry)).
6. ~~**Migrations card window**~~ — **Done:** [`migrations`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/migrations.scene.dry) now **`year >= 2302`** (was Jan–May 2300); problem/opportunity subscenes still need stack wiring if desired.
7. **Cable arc polish** — Close negotiation TODOs (tax → budget, disband flags); smoke-test syndicate timed events from a Jun 2301 deal through +1 / +3 months.
8. **Dundalk + orc events** — [`mss_dundalk_affair`](source/scenes/events/mss_dundalk_affair.scene.dry), [`orc_marriage1/2`](source/scenes/events/orc_marriage1.scene.dry) — verify electorate stacks and martyrs list integrate with [`status`](source/scenes/status.scene.dry) / future content.

9. **Implement [`mikasa_journey_inbound`](source/scenes/background/mikasa_journey_inbound.scene.dry)** — Short narrative + any flags needed before Titan (or remove hijack from [`post_event`](source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry) if unnecessary). Today it fires **before** Feb crisis and does nothing visible.
10. **Refugee prelude qualities** — Optionally add 2301 foreshadowing (library / peer media / status) referencing Jovian clan wars and kipple so Feb–Apr events aren't the first mention.
11. **Election coverage Jan 2300–Jan 2302** — Confirm [`runScheduledElections`](source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry) fires for all district months on calendar; player sees [`scheduled_elections`](source/scenes/events/scheduled_elections.scene.dry) at least twice before 2302.

### Phase D — Refugee crisis **start** (milestone deliverable)

12. **Verify Feb 2302 trigger** — [`refugees_titan`](source/scenes/major/refugees_titan.scene.dry): `jovian_refugee_prepare` / `jovian_refugee_dread` stacks already wired in [`electorate_runtime`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry); playtest that `third_wave_on_society = 1` unlocks third-wave prosperity row in [`status`](source/scenes/status.scene.dry).

        } else if (ELECTORATE_SCOPES[stackId]) {
            // legacy: (stackId, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])
            activeIf = delta
            delta = party
            party = target
            target = scope
            scope = stackId
            stackId = rowId
            this.gateWithActiveIf = arguments.length >= 6 && activeIf != null
        } else {
            this.gateWithActiveIf = arguments.length >= 7 && activeIf != null
        }
        this.id = rowId
        this.stackId = stackId || rowId
        this.scope = scope
        this.target = target || ''
        this.party = party
        this.delta = delta || 0
        this.activeIf = activeIf || function() { return true }
    }

    /** Stack count from Q[stackId]; non-numeric or <= 0 → no effect. */
    stacksFromQ(q) {
        if (!q || q[this.stackId] == null) { return 0 }
        var n = Number(q[this.stackId])
        if (isNaN(n) || n <= 0) { return 0 }
        return n
    }

    isActive(q) {
        try {
            return !!this.activeIf(q)
        } catch (e) {
            return false
        }
    }

    apply(state, q) {
        var stacks = this.stacksFromQ(q)
        if (stacks <= 0) { return }
        if (this.gateWithActiveIf && !this.isActive(q)) { return }
        var shift = this.delta * stacks
        if (this.scope === 'stratum') {
            var dem = state.demographicsById[this.target]
            if (dem) { electorateAddDelta(dem.competitiveScores, this.party, shift) }
        } else if (this.scope === 'district') {
            var dist = state.districtsById[this.target]
            if (dist) { electorateAddDelta(dist.competitiveScores, this.party, shift) }
        } else if (this.scope === 'global') {
            electorateAddDelta(state.global.competitiveScores, this.party, shift)
        }
    }
}

/** How radical the xenophobia is (0–1 linear, then sqrt above 1). Higher → harder for Dems to claw back. */
function effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad) {
    if (isNaN(rad) || rad <= 0) { return 0 }
    if (rad <= 1) { return rad }
    return Math.sqrt(rad)
}

/** Share of derived xenophobia Dems can claw off H (1 − radicalism, floored at 0). */
function demClawBackFraction(rad) {
    return Math.max(0, 1 - effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad))
}

/**
 * Derive modifier stacks from Q.parochialism (0–100).
 * xenophobia_derived: ramps above Suspicion (41+). H+/C− on 1st/2nd via catalog.
 * xenophobia_clawed_back: derived * demClawBackFraction(rad); C still hit by derived only.
 */
Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks = function(q) {
    q = q || Q
    var p = Number(q.parochialism)
    if (isNaN(p)) { p = 0 }
    var rad = Number(q.parochial_radicalism)
    if (isNaN(rad)) { rad = 0.65 }
    var clawMult = demClawBackFraction(rad)

    var suspicionFloor = 41
    var maxStack = 20
    var raw = p <= suspicionFloor ? 0 : ((p - suspicionFloor) / (100 - suspicionFloor)) * maxStack

    q.xenophobia_derived = raw
    q.xenophobia_clawed_back = raw * clawMult
}

    var state = Q.electionV2
    if (!state) { return }

    Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks(Q)

    state.demographicsById = state.demographicsById || Object.fromEntries(

    )
    state.districtsById = state.districtsById || Object.fromEntries(
        state.districts.map(function(d) { return [d.id, d] })
    )

    for (var j = 0; j < state.districts.length; j++) {

        dist.competitiveScores = electorateCopyScores(
            dist._baseCompetitiveScores || dist.competitiveScores
        )
    }

    /**

    constructor(rowId, stackId, scope, target, party, delta, activeIf) {

/** How radical the xenophobia is (0–1 linear, then sqrt above 1). Higher → harder for Dems to claw back. */
function effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad) {
    if (isNaN(rad) || rad <= 0) { return 0 }
    if (rad <= 1) { return rad }
    return Math.sqrt(rad)
}

/** Share of derived xenophobia Dems can claw off H (1 − radicalism, floored at 0). */
function demClawBackFraction(rad) {
    return Math.max(0, 1 - effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad))
}

/**
 * Derive modifier stacks from Q.parochialism (0–100).
 * xenophobia_derived: ramps above Suspicion (41+). H+/C− on 1st/2nd via catalog.
 * xenophobia_clawed_back: derived * demClawBackFraction(rad); C still hit by derived only.
 */
Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks = function(q) {
    q = q || Q
    var p = Number(q.parochialism)
    if (isNaN(p)) { p = 0 }
    var rad = Number(q.parochial_radicalism)
    if (isNaN(rad)) { rad = 0.65 }
    var clawMult = demClawBackFraction(rad)

    var suspicionFloor = 41
    var maxStack = 20
    var raw = p <= suspicionFloor ? 0 : ((p - suspicionFloor) / (100 - suspicionFloor)) * maxStack

    q.xenophobia_derived = raw
    q.xenophobia_clawed_back = raw * clawMult
}

Q.applyElectorateModifiers = function() {
    var state = Q.electionV2
    if (!state) { return }

    Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks(Q)

    state.demographicsById = state.demographicsById || Object.fromEntries(
        state.demographics.map(function(d) { return [d.id, d] })
    )
    state.districtsById = state.districtsById || Object.fromEntries(
        state.districts.map(function(d) { return [d.id, d] })
    )

    // Districts are not rebuilt by syncAllVoteAppeals; reset from baseline each poll.
    for (var j = 0; j < state.districts.length; j++) {
        var dist = state.districts[j]
        dist.competitiveScores = electorateCopyScores(
            dist._baseCompetitiveScores || dist.competitiveScores
        )
    }
    // Strata/global already base+appeals from election runtime sync; add stack deltas only.

    for (var m = 0; m < Q.electorateModifierCatalog.length; m++) {
        Q.electorateModifierCatalog[m].apply(state, Q)
    }
}

# Mikasa — implementation roadmap

Living inventory of what exists in `source/`, plus a plan to reach the **refugee crisis opening** ([`refugees_titan.scene.dry`](source/scenes/major/refugees_titan.scene.dry), February 2302).

**Monthly loop:** [`advance.scene.dry`](source/scenes/advance.scene.dry) → [`post_event.scene.dry`](source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry) (tick + `#event` queue) → [`main.scene.dry`](source/scenes/main.scene.dry).

**New game:** [`root.scene.dry`](source/scenes/root.scene.dry) `@start` → runtime bootstrap [`setup_functions.scene.dry`](source/scenes/setup_functions.scene.dry) → [`main.scene.dry`](source/scenes/main.scene.dry). Prologue text continues at [`root.scene.dry`](source/scenes/root.scene.dry) `@2300_main_continue` → [`organize_phase_start.scene.dry`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_start.scene.dry).

---

## Background / runtime mechanics

These scenes load once (or each boot), define APIs on `Q`, and are not player-facing cards.

| Mechanic | Scene | Notes |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Boot orchestration | [`setup_functions.scene.dry`](source/scenes/setup_functions.scene.dry) | Chains runtime scenes until election, electorate, economic, attitude, and organize APIs exist. |
| Election v2 (tabulation, seats, projections) | [`election_runtime.scene.dry`](source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry) | Source of truth for voter blocks, districts, IG boosts. Dev mirror: `source/lib/election-v2.js`. |
| Electorate modifier catalog | [`electorate_runtime.scene.dry`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry) | `ElectorateModifier` rows; stacks from story choices (`dundalk_*`, contracts, cable neg, refugee prep, …). |

on-arrival: {!

// MIKASA_ELECTORATE_RUNTIME_BEGIN
// --- Electorate modifiers (applied after vote-label sync in Q.update_projections) ---
// stackId: Q quality bumped in events (e.g. favor_second_wave_housing_dispute += 1).
// Several rows may share one stackId (multiple effects per choice).
// Dendry initializes missing qualities to 0 before +=. Each poll applies delta * stacks.
// Scopes: stratum (demographic), district (region), global.

var ELECTORATE_PARTY_KEYS = ['D', 'I', 'C', 'G', 'H']

function electorateZeroScores() {
    return { D: 0, I: 0, C: 0, G: 0, H: 0 }
}

function electorateCopyScores(src) {
    var out = electorateZeroScores()
    for (var i = 0; i < ELECTORATE_PARTY_KEYS.length; i++) {
        var k = ELECTORATE_PARTY_KEYS[i]
        out[k] = (src && src[k]) || 0
    }
    return out
}

function electorateAddDelta(scores, party, delta) {
    if (scores && scores[party] !== undefined) {
        scores[party] += delta
    }
}

var ELECTORATE_SCOPES = { stratum: 1, district: 1, global: 1 }

class ElectorateModifier {
    /**
     * Positional (table-friendly):
     *   new ElectorateModifier(rowId, stackId, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])
     *   new ElectorateModifier(stackId, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])  // legacy: rowId = stackId
     * stackId: Q quality for stacks (favor_second_wave_housing_dispute += 1).
     * scope: 'stratum' | 'district' | 'global' — use '' for target when global.
     * Object form: { id, stackId?, scope, target, party, delta, activeIf? }
     */
    constructor(rowId, stackId, scope, target, party, delta, activeIf) {
        var fromObject = rowId && typeof rowId === 'object'
        if (fromObject) {
            var opts = rowId
            rowId = opts.id
            stackId = opts.stackId != null ? opts.stackId : opts.id
            scope = opts.scope
            target = opts.target
            party = opts.party
            delta = opts.delta
            activeIf = opts.activeIf
            this.gateWithActiveIf = activeIf != null
        } else if (ELECTORATE_SCOPES[stackId]) {
            // legacy: (stackId, scope, target, party, delta [, activeIf])
            activeIf = delta
            delta = party
            party = target
            target = scope
            scope = stackId
            stackId = rowId
            this.gateWithActiveIf = arguments.length >= 6 && activeIf != null
        } else {
            this.gateWithActiveIf = arguments.length >= 7 && activeIf != null
        }
        this.id = rowId
        this.stackId = stackId || rowId
        this.scope = scope
        this.target = target || ''
        this.party = party
        this.delta = delta || 0
        this.activeIf = activeIf || function() { return true }
    }

    /** Stack count from Q[stackId]; non-numeric or <= 0 → no effect. */
    stacksFromQ(q) {
        if (!q || q[this.stackId] == null) { return 0 }
        var n = Number(q[this.stackId])
        if (isNaN(n) || n <= 0) { return 0 }
        return n
    }

    isActive(q) {
        try {
            return !!this.activeIf(q)
        } catch (e) {
            return false
        }
    }

    apply(state, q) {
        var stacks = this.stacksFromQ(q)
        if (stacks <= 0) { return }
        if (this.gateWithActiveIf && !this.isActive(q)) { return }
        var shift = this.delta * stacks
        if (this.scope === 'stratum') {
            var dem = state.demographicsById[this.target]
            if (dem) { electorateAddDelta(dem.competitiveScores, this.party, shift) }
        } else if (this.scope === 'district') {
            var dist = state.districtsById[this.target]
            if (dist) { electorateAddDelta(dist.competitiveScores, this.party, shift) }
        } else if (this.scope === 'global') {
            electorateAddDelta(state.global.competitiveScores, this.party, shift)
        }
    }
}

/** How radical the xenophobia is (0–1 linear, then sqrt above 1). Higher → harder for Dems to claw back. */
function effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad) {
    if (isNaN(rad) || rad <= 0) { return 0 }
    if (rad <= 1) { return rad }
    return Math.sqrt(rad)
}

/** Share of derived xenophobia Dems can claw off H (1 − radicalism, floored at 0). */
function demClawBackFraction(rad) {
    return Math.max(0, 1 - effectiveParochialRadicalism(rad))
}

/**
 * Derive modifier stacks from Q.parochialism (0–100).
 * xenophobia_derived: ramps above Suspicion (41+). H+/C− on 1st/2nd via catalog.
 * xenophobia_clawed_back: derived * demClawBackFraction(rad); C still hit by derived only.
 */
Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks = function(q) {
    q = q || Q
    var p = Number(q.parochialism)
    if (isNaN(p)) { p = 0 }
    var rad = Number(q.parochial_radicalism)
    if (isNaN(rad)) { rad = 0.65 }
    var clawMult = demClawBackFraction(rad)

    var suspicionFloor = 41
    var maxStack = 20
    var raw = p <= suspicionFloor ? 0 : ((p - suspicionFloor) / (100 - suspicionFloor)) * maxStack

    q.xenophobia_derived = raw
    q.xenophobia_clawed_back = raw * clawMult
}

Q.applyElectorateModifiers = function() {
    var state = Q.electionV2
    if (!state) { return }

    Q.syncParochialismXenophobiaStacks(Q)

    state.demographicsById = state.demographicsById || Object.fromEntries(
        state.demographics.map(function(d) { return [d.id, d] })
    )
    state.districtsById = state.districtsById || Object.fromEntries(
        state.districts.map(function(d) { return [d.id, d] })
    )

    // Districts are not rebuilt by syncAllVoteAppeals; reset from baseline each poll.
    for (var j = 0; j < state.districts.length; j++) {
        var dist = state.districts[j]
        dist.competitiveScores = electorateCopyScores(
            dist._baseCompetitiveScores || dist.competitiveScores
        )
    }
    // Strata/global already base+appeals from election runtime sync; add stack deltas only.

    for (var m = 0; m < Q.electorateModifierCatalog.length; m++) {
        Q.electorateModifierCatalog[m].apply(state, Q)
    }
}

Updated `drone_vote_buying.dry` to use the ElectorateModifier stack pattern:

**Useful** — `drone_syndicate_bribe_boost = 1` → **+0.2 G** on the `drone` stratum  
**Troubling** — `drone_corp_bribe_slip = 1` → **−0.1 C** on the `drone` stratum  

Because drones use the `corp_or_abstain` rule, only **C** votes count; D/G/H/I ballot weight becomes abstention. So:

- Higher **G** appeal → more ballot mass assigned to G → zeroed out → **higher abstention %**, lower corp share (modest effect)
- Lower **C** appeal → fewer counted corp votes → **higher abstention %** with a smaller shift (troubling path)

Both show up on the status screen as `drone_poll_C` vs `drone_poll_abstain`. Lint passes.
is there a framework in place that would allow the "useful" choice to also add a small number of drones to the syndicate interest group?
The full context is now clear. This is an informational question, so no code changes are needed unless the user requests implementation.

**Not yet** — there’s no implemented way to move a specific number of drones into a syndicate IG from an event choice.

## What exists today

IG membership is **fixed at boot** as a **national share per stratum**, not a headcount you can bump:

```121:128:source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry
    Families: {
        rich: 0.02, first: 0.04, second: 0.08, coop: 0.01, drone: 0.01,
    },
    Edges: {
        rich: 0.01, first: 0.05, second: 0.07, coop: 0.01, drone: 0.01,
    },
    Sharks: {
        rich: 0.01, first: 0.03, second: 0.1, drone: 0.01,
    },
```

Each syndicate IG then computes ballots as  
`block.population × effectiveMembership(block)` (share × district home boost, capped by `igClaimCap`). Drones already have syndicate shares (1% each), but nothing in events can add “+500 drones to Families.”

The **“useful”** path you have now uses **ElectorateModifier** — it raises **G appeal on the drone stratum**, which under `corp_or_abstain` shows up as **more abstentions**, not more syndicate members:

```771:775:source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry
/** Non-Corp ballots abstain (not counted); Corp (C) unchanged. */
function corpOrAbstainPartyVotes(votes) {
    const out = zeroPartyVotes()
    out.C = votes.C || 0
    return out
}
```

That’s poll/competitive behavior, not IG roster size.

## What’s planned but not built

[`source/scenes/planning/ig_demographics.txt`](source/scenes/planning/ig_demographics.txt) describes the intended system: per–voter-block `ig_membership[ig]` headcounts, monthly recompute of `non_ig_population`, and event effects that transfer people stratum → IG. **None of that is wired in `election_runtime` yet.**

## Practical options

| Approach | Status |
|--------|--------|
| **ElectorateModifier** (drone G↑ / C↓) | **Implemented** — shifts abstention display |
| **Stack → bump IG membership share** (e.g. `families_drone_membership += 0.001`) | **Not implemented** — would need runtime API + catalog rows |
| **Per-block headcount transfer** (planning doc) | **Not implemented** |
| **Raw JS** mutating `Q.electionV2.interestGroups[n].membership` in `on-arrival` | Possible but **ad hoc**, no stack pattern, easy to desync from CLI mirror |

So for “useful adds a small number of drones to the syndicate,” you’d need new election-runtime support (membership modifier stacks or the full `ig_demographics` model). The closest live substitute is what you already have: more drone weight toward G → more abstention in general-population polls, without changing syndicate IG population counts.

If you want this wired up, the lightest path is probably membership-modifier stacks on `InterestGroup.effectiveMembership()` (parallel to `ElectorateModifier`), before the heavier per-block conversion system.
for now, can you make the event increase their drone membership shares from 0.01 to 0.015 and put a note that this should be revised when ig_memberships get overhauled?
I'll add `Q.applySyndicateDroneMembershipBribe` near `update_projections` and include a comment noting that `ig_memberships` needs revising later.

priority: 5

The employment contracts of Megacorporation employees in Mikasa generally forbid them to vote for candidates the corporation deems unacceptable.  Consequently the only choice is between voting as their employeer wants and abstaining.  The Megacorps induce their employees not to abstain with financial and workplace incentives.

It seems that the syndiates have decided it's worth counter bribing the drones, paying them not to vote.  This would shift the electorate for general population elections in favor of other candiates, including the ones the syndicates bribe or pressure people into supporting.  The effect would be most strongly felt in the districts with the main corporate strongholds, the Railyard, Limelight and Vats.

### Phase A — Core loop hygiene (blocking)

1. ~~**Advance `phase` beyond 1**~~ — **Done:** [`cable_break_negotiations`](source/scenes/major/cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry) sets `phase = 2` when ≥2 megacorps accept the ceasefire (Jun 2301). Optionally tie [`organize_phase_tick`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) trade-level `phase` bands to calendar elsewhere.
2. ~~**Remove SPD leftovers**~~ — **Done:** deleted [`shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry`](source/scenes/cards/city_affairs/shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry). **Next:** design a `#city_affairs` card to renegotiate corp control of civil rights, judiciary, and related government levers (see table above).
3. **Fix [`organize_phase_start`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_start.scene.dry) entry** — Either gate it to Jan 2300 month 1 (first `post_event`) or chain explicitly from [`root`](source/scenes/root.scene.dry) `@2300_main_continue` so `organizing_unlock` is guaranteed before October events.
4. **Date-gate [`drone_vote_buying`](source/scenes/background/drone_vote_buying.dry)** — Add `year`, `max-visits`, or remove until designed; avoid firing every December forever.

### Phase B — 2300–2301 story spine (content)

5. ~~**September Convention fallout**~~ — **Done:** [`september_convention`](source/scenes/events/september_convention.scene.dry) permit bumps `parochialism`; ban cuts `parochialism` / `parochial_radicalism` and stacks `first_wave_ban_slights` (first-stratum poll modifiers in [`electorate_runtime`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry)).
6. ~~**Migrations card window**~~ — **Done:** [`migrations`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/migrations.scene.dry) now **`year >= 2302`** (was Jan–May 2300); problem/opportunity subscenes still need stack wiring if desired.
7. **Cable arc polish** — Close negotiation TODOs (tax → budget, disband flags); smoke-test syndicate timed events from a Jun 2301 deal through +1 / +3 months.
8. ~~**Dundalk + orc events**~~ — **Done (orc):** [`orc_marriage2`](source/scenes/events/orc_marriage2.scene.dry) sets `orc_marriage_*` stacks; stratum poll shifts in [`electorate_runtime`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry). Dundalk stacks already wired; verify martyrs in [`status`](source/scenes/status.scene.dry) if needed.

### Phase C — Bridge to 2302 (refugee runway)

9. **Implement [`mikasa_journey_inbound`](source/scenes/background/mikasa_journey_inbound.scene.dry)** — Short narrative + any flags needed before Titan (or remove hijack from [`post_event`](source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry) if unnecessary). Today it fires **before** Feb crisis and does nothing visible.
10. **Refugee prelude qualities** — Optionally add 2301 foreshadowing (library / peer media / status) referencing Jovian clan wars and kipple so Feb–Apr events aren't the first mention.
11. **Election coverage Jan 2300–Jan 2302** — Confirm [`runScheduledElections`](source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry) fires for all district months on calendar; player sees [`scheduled_elections`](source/scenes/events/scheduled_elections.scene.dry) at least twice before 2302.

### Phase D — Refugee crisis **start** (milestone deliverable)

12. **Verify Feb 2302 trigger** — [`refugees_titan`](source/scenes/major/refugees_titan.scene.dry): `jovian_refugee_prepare` / `jovian_refugee_dread` stacks already wired in [`electorate_runtime`](source/scenes/electorate_runtime.scene.dry); playtest that `third_wave_on_society = 1` unlocks third-wave prosperity row in [`status`](source/scenes/status.scene.dry).
13. **Minimal follow-through for Mar–Apr** — Expand [`refugees_earth`](source/scenes/major/refugees_earth.scene.dry) and [`refugees_otherworld`](source/scenes/major/refugees_otherworld.scene.dry) with at least one meaningful stack or budget/housing pressure each (crisis **continues**, but start is Feb Titan).
14. **Smoke test full timeline** — Dev cheat or `npm run`-style month advance: 2300-01 → 2302-02 in one session; no JS errors; main deck always has Advance; organizing cards appear after unlock.

### Phase E — Nice-to-have before playtesting wider (non-blocking for “crisis start”)

- **Add district crime formula** — monthly tick + standard crime modifier stack; prosperity down, syndicate membership/prosperity up (syndicate × district); hook police ([`security`](source/scenes/cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry)), militia, and [`community_outreach`](source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry).
- Wire [`corp_conflict`](source/scenes/background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) into monthly tick while `cable_break_peace = 0`.
- Enable `#advisor` deck with Mikasa conditions.
- Hook [`industries/mining`](source/scenes/industries/mining.scene.dry) into organizing or city deck.
- Third-wave voter blocks in [`election_runtime`](source/scenes/election_runtime.scene.dry) if elections should shift after `third_wave_on_society`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Phase A: loop hygiene] --> B[Phase B: 2300-2301 spine]
  B --> C[Phase C: 2302 bridge]
  C --> D[Phase D: refugees_titan milestone]
  D --> E[Phase E: polish]
```

Done. The **useful** choice now:

1. Keeps `drone_syndicate_bribe_boost = 1` (drone stratum G↑ → more abstentions)
2. Calls `Q.applySyndicateDroneMembershipBribe()` — sets **Families, Edges, and Sharks** drone membership share to **0.015** (from baseline **0.01**)

The helper lives in `election_runtime.scene.dry` with a comment pointing at the future `ig_demographics.txt` per-block system. The event file has a matching `# TODO` note, and the roadmap row documents the temporary approach.

Lint passes. After picking useful, syndicate IG ballots from drone blocks should tick up slightly on the next projection pass.

let's have a simple action economy.
Every month the player gains 1 action.
Up to 4 unused actions carry forward.
Of the actions currently available, up to two can be used in a month by default or 3 can be used if no action was used last month.
The action reserve and monthly actions available both get shown on the politics page, the monthly reserve shows as x/4

Then the various cards for community organizing stuff (including militias) will have an action cost added to all their choices except for return to hand and will be disabled if there aren't any actions left that month.
Planning the action economy system.

Starting with the action economy core, then updating the cards.

Mapping out which cards cost actions. Leaf choices need choose-if and spend logic. Top-level menus like @big_3 stay free. Adding the action economy JavaScript block to organize_phase_tick.scene.dry. Updating main.scene to sync the display on arrival. Refreshing the ORGANIZE_API list.

A runtime hook to auto-gate choices isn't possible without engine changes, so I'm patching each card file directly. Every leaf choice gets a `choose-if` check against remaining monthly actions, plus an `on-arrival` spend routine. Existing conditions will be combined with `and`. After spending, I'll trigger a sync across the main scene and status politics page.

Monthly actions remaining equals the lower of the usage limit and the reserve. Recalculating from raw values avoids extra sync calls after each spend. Need to verify whether main scene on-arrival triggers when a player returns to a card from hand, since scene recompilation may skip it.

Since returning from a subscene may leave the player on the same card, root-level on-arrival sync is unreliable. I'll add a display-sync call to each organizing card's on-arrival instead, and also trigger it inside the spend routine. Cards that don't spend at root will rely on the per-card sync.

Realized that updating `action_reserve` and `month_actions_used` during on-arrival leaves `month_actions_remaining` stale until the main scene refreshes. The `spendOrganizingAction` helper must recalculate and update that value directly.

Decided to centralize action spending through a `Q.spendOrganizingAction()` helper that updates the reserve and monthly usage, then calls `syncActionEconomyDisplay()` to refresh the remaining count. This keeps inline on-arrival scripts tidy and avoids fragile manual sync calls.

Decided to use `spendOrganizingAction` for every card that spends actions. A bare semicolon block would risk spending without checking `choose-if`, and manually subtracting from `month_actions_remaining` is wrong because the remaining count must be recalculated from the raw reserve and monthly usage. The helper handles the correct calculation inline.

= Community Conflicts

The corporate dominated government allows local conflicts and disputes to fester.  If anything they find the a divided community advantageous.  We dont necessarily need government powers to fix every problem, the democratic movement has attracted respected figures from the various communities who can mediate disputes and promote unity throughout the city.

- @first_wave_community
- @second_wave_community
- @isolated_communities
- @drones_community
- @otherworlders_community
- @return

@first_wave_community
title: Calm the first wave settlers
subtitle: Japanese, European, American
choose-if: community_first_wave_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: First-wave conflicts already mediated.
on-arrival: community_first_wave_resolved = 1; first_wave_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_first_wave += 1

The first settlers were Japanese, whose numbers were joined by European and American colonists.  They are some of the best established and most prosperous people of Mikasa but the rivalries created by the chaos on earth leads to resentments in space, both between each other and towards the more recent arrivals.

The various kinship networks and cooperatives of the first wave have countless petty disputes, some of which stretch back over a century.  From time to time they have negotiated compromises on old contracts or grudges.  We encourage them to get these affairs back in order.


@second_wave_community
title: Stabilize second wave communities
subtitle: Bantu, Middle Eastern, Southeastern Asian
choose-if: community_second_wave_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Second-wave conflicts already mediated.
on-arrival: community_second_wave_resolved = 1; second_wave_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_second_wave += 1

Mikasa and the other transsolar waystations became refugee destinations as the conflicts on Earth and the Jovian Moons worsened.  Many of the refugees came from places that had no previous ties to Mikasa.  The corporations were eager to have them come to serve as cheap labor but unconcerned with sustainable living conditions.  Uprooted from their existing support networks they have struggled but over time new communities are emerging.

Addressing shortfalls in Mikasa's infrastructure and making connections with local community leaders helps address the poor living conditions and conflicts among these groups.

@isolated_communities
title: Outreach to isolated communities
subtitle: Deepers and Tunnel Clans
choose-if: community_isolated_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Isolated communities already reached.
on-arrival: community_isolated_resolved = 1; isolated_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_isolated += 1

The deepers are a community that originally settled on a different site of the asteroid from the tether ground station.  They intensely resent their annexation and desire a return to autonomy.  The tunnel clans are communities that left the artificial gravity grid and hid themselves away deep in the embrace of the "mother".  Their technical savviness could be an asset if we could overcome their isolation but this will be difficult as they can take care of their own and have little need for us.

@drones_community
title: Make inroads among the corporate employees
subtitle: Hereditary worker caste
choose-if: community_drones_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Drone-community outreach already done.
on-arrival: community_drones_resolved = 1; drones_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_drones += 1

Most corporate employees on Mikasa work for the Big Three, Community Soylent, Magrail Combine and Brazos Universal.  Corporate employeeship has become a hereditary caste that jealously guards their privledges and relative wealth over the underclass.

Any efforts to reach out to this group will inevitably be called illegal labor organizing.  Still there are more daring employees who have learned to keep things off the bosses radar.  Off the books mutual aid networks will help the conditions of the drones even if only a little.


@otherworlders_community
title: Assimilate arrivals from the otherworld
subtitle: Ruukish (otherworld humans), Fae, Orcs
choose-if: community_otherworld_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Otherworlder conflicts already mediated.
on-arrival: community_otherworld_resolved = 1; otherworld_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_otherworld += 1

Although small in number, the refugees from the mystic otherworld have extreme culture shock.  What's worse they have brought a bitter ethnic conflict with them, the Orci question.  The orcs are often conflated with the orci, magical immitations of life while the fae are accused of ensnaring others in their magics.  The otherworld humans who typically are at the bottom of the heirarchy in the otherworld resent both groups but have trouble adjusting to a technological existence when they rarely possess basic literacy.

We can help educate the otherworlders in our ways, hopefullly learning from the times humanity has put aside it's conflicts instead of allowing them to fester.  And in turn we might learn more of the magical arts of the otherworld.  Even if few of the refugees were trained in the magical arts, they have seen far more magic then the vast majority of people from this world.

title: Make inroads among the corporate employees
subtitle: Hereditary worker caste
choose-if: community_drones_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Drone-community outreach already done.
on-arrival: community_drones_resolved = 1; drones_cohesion += 1; crime_relief_drones += 1

Any efforts to reach out to this group will inevitably be called illegal labor organizing.  Still there are more daring employees who have learned to keep things off the bosses radar.  Off the books mutual aid networks will help the conditions of the drones even if only a little.


@otherworlders_community
title: Assimilate arrivals from the otherworld
subtitle: Ruukish (otherworld humans), Fae, Orcs
choose-if: community_otherworld_resolved = 0
unavailable-subtitle: Otherworlder conflicts already mediated.

Although small in number, the refugees from the mystic otherworld have extreme culture shock.  What's worse they have brought a bitter ethnic conflict with them, the Orci question.  The orcs are often conflated with the orci, magical immitations of life while the fae are accused of ensnaring others in their magics.  The otherworld humans who typically are at the bottom of the heirarchy in the otherworld resent both groups but have trouble adjusting to a technological existence when they rarely possess basic literacy.

We can help educate the otherworlders in our ways, hopefullly learning from the times humanity has put aside it's conflicts instead of allowing them to fester.  And in turn we might learn more of the magical arts of the otherworld.  Even if few of the refugees were trained in the magical arts, they have seen far more magic then the vast majority of people from this world.

title: Education and training
new-page: true
is-card: true
card-image: img/asteroid.jpg
tags: local_organizing, city_affairs
view_if: organizing_unlock = 1

The education system has both greatly advanced and greatly regressed since the pre-spaceflight era.  On the positive side, ubiquitous open sourced computerized educational resources have made it trivial for parents to provide children with basic life skills. On the negative side, most children are not recieving formal schooling.  Unschooled children are often left unprepared to the workforce and ignorant of world affairs.  The problem is particularly severe among the non-human populations from the otherworld.

-@too_broke: We dont have the resources right now
-@vocational
-@home_ec
-@well_rounded
- @return

@vocational
title: Focus on vocational training to reduce poverty
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.
on-arrival: {! Q.spendOrganizingAction(); Q.vocational_track += 1; !}

Improving vocational training helps workers get better jobs, in particular with the corporations.  School attendence has risen somewhat as students are attracted by the prospect of higher incomes.  The megacorps approve of this curriculum and agree to contract some of their internal training programs over to our education system which allows us to offset the costs of this expansion.

title: Expand teaching of home economics skills like nutrition, health, electronics and mechanics
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.

We strive to give students the skills to be more self reliant, making their food nuYen go farther, preventing health complications and repairing their home goods instead of buying new ones.  The cooperatives approve of this curriculum and some of their home schooled students have started attending classes part time.

title: Provide a well rounded education
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.
on-arrival: {! Q.spendOrganizingAction(); !}

We are laying the foundation for a true public education system.  This is an expensive choice but will improve education outcomes across the board in the long term.  This is particularly beneficial for the otherworld population.

title: Media ideology 
new-page: true
is-card: true
card-image: img/asteroid.jpg
tags: local_organizing
on-arrival: {! if (typeof Q.syncActionEconomyDisplay === 'function') { Q.syncActionEconomyDisplay() } !}

There are few proper outlets on Mikasa, the corporations shut down any independent competition with their propoganda that is too successful.  A handful of small outlets get by under the radar of the megacorps but most independent journalists rely on annonymous online peer to peer networks to get their reporting out.  Since most members of this small community follow each other's stories, the zeitgeist of the underground media shifts from time to time.

Depending on what topics the underground is most interested in, different groups might become politically active.  What topics is the underground covering?

-@labor
-@wealthy
-@diplomatic
- @return

@labor
title: Abusive working conditions and the need for worker protections
subtitle: Popular among the poor and pisses off nobody but the megacorps
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.
on-arrival: {! Q.spendOrganizingAction(); Q.anti_corp_media += 1; !}

Populist rhetoric is an easy way to get people wanting change.  The Stakeholder revolt might have been crushed but plenty of people are stakeholders in everything but name.

@wealthy
title: stress the need for self sufficiency and protection of businesses
subtitle: High skilled workers and cooperatives would like this but the establishment tone would be offputting to workers
view-if: self_sufficiency_media = 0
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.
on-arrival: {! Q.spendOrganizingAction(); Q.self_sufficiency_media += 1; !}

Terrestrials or Martians might be surprised that discussions on IP restrictions on agrinutritional growth mediums can draw an audience but the matter is literally a matter of life and death for many in the cooperatives.  The wealthy usually are hostile towards the cooperatives but the discussion creates some cross-class solidarity, at least among the non-shareholder wealthy.

@diplomatic
title: discussion of Mikasa's place in the solar system economy and negotiations with megacorps
subtitle: We might be able to negotiate with corps in good faith, but any economic compromise would undermine self sufficiency
choose-if: month_actions_remaining > 0
unavailable-subtitle: No organizing actions left this month.
on-arrival: {! Q.spendOrganizingAction(); Q.kiss_ass_media += 1; !}

Most people aren't interested in solarpolitical theory crafting but the podcast crowd keeps talking about it.  It doesn't move the needle on public opinion but maybe some good ideas will emerge from it.

Core logic in `organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`:

```930:945:source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry
/** Month-start: +1 reserve (cap 4), reset used, set limit 2 or 3 if idle last month. */
Q.beginActionEconomyMonth = function() {
    var usedLast = Number(Q.month_actions_used) || 0
    Q.actions_used_last_month = usedLast
    Q.month_actions_used = 0
    Q.month_actions_limit = (usedLast === 0) ? 3 : 2
    var reserve = Number(Q.action_reserve) || 0
    if (reserve < 0) { reserve = 0 }
    Q.action_reserve = Math.min(ACTION_RESERVE_MAX, reserve + 1)
    return syncActionEconomyDisplay()
}

function monthly_tick_phase1() {
    if (typeof Q.beginActionEconomyMonth === 'function') {
        Q.beginActionEconomyMonth()
    }
```

2. Resets `month_actions_used` to **0**

Here’s what was causing the blank flashes — they’re **silent setup/routing scenes** with no prose, not broken content.

### On startup (before `organize_phase_start`)

Two culprits, often the same flash:

1. **`organize_phase_tick`** — Bootstrap loads runtime APIs here (`max-visits: 1`, `new-page: false`, no body text). It was **missing `go-to: jumpScene`**, unlike every other runtime scene, so the engine could **stop on this blank page** instead of returning to `setup_functions`.

2. **`root.2300_main_continue`** — After bootstrap, `setup_functions` jumped here, which only contained `go-to: organize_phase_start` and no content. The “2300” intro prose in `root.scene.dry` sits **after** that `go-to`, so it never displayed.

text: I found the smoking gun.

Your memory matches the old Weimar-style pattern. Here’s what changed.

### How it used to work

The “dark time” block lives on `root.2300_main_continue` in `root.scene.dry`:

```154:161:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
@2300_main_continue
go-to: organize_phase_start

= 2300 

It is a dark time for humanity.  Earth is mired in endless national conflicts while the off planet colonies are torn by violence between lawless corporations.

As the corporations of the interplanetary waystation Mikasa become too distracted fighting each other, real power has started to fall into the hands of the city government for the first time in decades.  Now our task is to somehow maintain this newfound autonomy while beating back corruption.  Perhaps Mikasa might one day control the corporations instead of the other way around.
```

That mirrors the old `@1928_main` → `go-to: main` flow: show the year heading and intro prose, then enter the hand scene.

For that to appear **above the decks on main**, `main` must **not** clear the page. Originally `main.scene.dry` had no `new-page:` (there was even a `# TODO: should this really be a new page?` comment). With `new-page: false`, Dendry **appends** main’s hand UI below whatever `2300_main_continue` just rendered — so the intro stayed visible above the cards.

### Why it stopped

**1. `new-page: true` on `main` (May 25, commit `8dde925`)**

Adding `new-page: true` to `main` makes every arrival call `$content.empty()` before drawing the hand. The intro from `2300_main_continue` is wiped as soon as main loads, even if bootstrap still visits that scene first.

**2. Bootstrap destination changed (May 26, commit `303e172`)**

`2300_main_continue` was changed from `go-to: main` to `go-to: organize_phase_start`. First landing after bootstrap became the political-situation event, not main — so the intro–main pairing broke even if it had still been visible.

**3. Bootstrap skip (recent blank-scene fix)**

`setup_functions` now jumps straight to `organize_phase_start`, so `root.2300_main_continue` never runs and the intro never displays at all.

### Summary

| When | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Originally | `2300_main_continue` shows intro → `main` (no `new-page`) → intro stays above hand |
| May 25 `8dde925` | `main` gets `new-page: true` → intro cleared on first main visit |
| May 26 `303e172` | Bootstrap goes to `organize_phase_start` instead of `main` |
| Recent | Bootstrap skips `2300_main_continue` entirely |

The prose is still in source and still compiles onto `root.2300_main_continue`; it’s the routing and `new-page: true` on `main` that prevent it from showing above the hand.

If you want it back, sensible options are: put the intro in `main.scene.dry` behind a one-shot flag (`main_intro_seen`), restore the `2300_main_continue` hop and drop `new-page` on first main visit only, or show it on `organize_phase_start` before the political text. I can implement whichever you prefer.
